inputs.xtext_rule_text:
OwnedFeatureInverting returns SysML::FeatureInverting :
	  invertingFeature = [SysML::Feature | QualifiedName]
	| ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain
;

decision: As KerML 8.2.4.3.6 states it: the inverting feature, either as a cross-reference `[QualifiedName]`, which parses a QualifiedName, or as an owned feature chain. The `{ ownedRelatedElement += ... }` action consumes no tokens. The Xtext states the same two alternatives. Both alternatives can begin with a name, so a parser decides between them after it. Neither QualifiedName nor OwnedFeatureChain is defined in this clause, so exactly where they diverge is for their own units to establish.

evidence.note: OwnedFeatureInverting : FeatureInverting = invertingFeature = [QualifiedName] | invertingFeature = OwnedFeatureChain { ownedRelatedElement += invertingFeature }

line 14: `feature gg : A featured by B inverse of A::f;`, the QualifiedName alternative. No corpus model inverts a feature chain (`inverse of a.b`); that alternative rests on the clause and the Xtext.
OwnedFeatureInverting: invertingFeature = [SysML::Feature | QualifiedName] | ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain. Agrees.

notes: re-scoped (ADR-0015): only the kerml grammar reaches this production, so its work now lives in OwnedFeatureInverting@kerml
